survivingClaim: Precise obstruction stands in narrowed form. Gonek's stage P_X + chi conj(P_X) has all zeros on the line for any non-vanishing P_X, so the on-line property carries no arithmetic (every unimodular twist passes; DH and T-NR fail only at non-vanishing). The degree (Rouche) inequality zeta/G_X not in (-inf,0] on a box boundary implies the box is zero-free, so no statement strictly weaker than zero-freeness of the boxes implies it; at fixed X it fails at arbitrarily large heights for sigma_0<1 (Montgomery, recalled). The boundary quantity is log zeta - log P_X - log(1+Theta). For the Fejer weight, F_Y'(t) = 2 log Y sum_rho Re kappa((rho-s) log Y) - 2 Re[Y^(1-s)/((1-s)^2 log Y)] + O(1/t) (classical explicit formula, numerically confirmed at several heights), giving F_Y' >= -small under RH for Y up to a power of t. Two boxes near T=1e6 certified in ball arithmetic, below verified height. Not established: non-locality in "any height / half-plane" form, the shifted Thm 5.1 sandwich and threshold, any general no-go for the approximate functional equation. No statement about zeros of zeta beyond verified height.
obstruction: Gonek's stage P_X + chi conj(P_X) has all zeros on the line for any non-vanishing P_X: the on-line property contains no arithmetic. The Rouche (degree) inequality zeta/G_X not in (-inf,0] on a box boundary implies the box is zero-free and is implied (Gonek Thm 5.1) only by zero-freeness at sigma_0 - C loglog t/log X; nothing strictly weaker implies it, and at fixed X it fails at arbitrarily large height (Montgomery, recalled). The boundary quantity log zeta - log P_X - log(1+Theta) is a sum over all zeros; the approximate functional equation re-expresses it. With Fejer weights the k = 0 comb term is the Weil functional on Fejer tests (rows P10/eq48). Not established: non-locality in half-plane form (step 4), any general no-go for the approximate functional equation.

lesson: A stage whose zeros are on the line by construction (functional equation as input) carries no information in that property: it holds for any non-vanishing P, including U. All content sits in the comparison zeta/stage, which at fixed distance from the line is the Hurwitz comparison zeta/P_X (c1 Thm. D), and whose prime-side form is a two-sided bound on the prime tail beyond X at abscissa below 1 (Landau target, twisted local form). The FE term has modulus (t/2pi)^(-d); in the layer d <= 1/L it helps short products (X=2: 0 vs 76 crossings in 2000 units) and lowers the measured margin for X >= 100. Lead 13 is not answered: U fails only at the step that is the conclusion.
